key_insight: SUAF compresses action-dependent predictions of future visitation into leading spectral features that support reward-independent, zero-shot policy improvement.
engineering_relevance: Agents can reuse learned features across reward functions, with spectral truncation providing a principled way to manage representation capacity and approximation error.
method: Construct an action-centered, positive-lag canonical dependence matrix under a reference policy.
Retain leading singular modes to approximate delayed advantages through linear reward projections, keeping immediate reward contrasts separate.
Learn features from reward-free data using action-centered Soft-HGR and bidirectional temporal-difference estimation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports finite-state validation of spectral predictions and feature learning, plus zero-shot evaluations on discrete tasks and continuous-control benchmarks, without quantitative results.
watch_item: Policy-improvement guarantees require sufficient error conditions; retaining leading modes alone does not guarantee improvement for every reward.
paper_title: SUAF: Spectral Universal Advantage Features for Zero-Shot Policy Improvement
